articles.title: Watch: SIR row: ECI to re-issue enumeration forms to those off draft rolls | Above the Fold | Nov 6, 2026
articles.description: The Election Commission has said that voters who did not submit their Enumeration Forms during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls can still submit them. The forms will be regenerated, and voters will have to explain why they missed the initial submission. Also in focus: The Supreme Court flags Delhi’s worsening air pollution ahead of Deepavali; the Jharkhand High Court quashes the State government’s decision to cancel the JSSC-CGL recruitment exam; Gadi Eisenkot emerges as a potential candidate to form Israel’s next government; and Indian-born Nithya Raman wins the Los Angeles mayoral race.

articles.description: Deepotsav is celebrated in Ayodhya, marking Lord Shri Ram's return and symbolizing cultural pride and global attention. This festival has evolved into a grand event showcasing India's traditions and modern technologies. The focus on local artisans and products aims to revive traditional crafts and enhance the local economy. The state government emphasizes the connection between faith, security, and opportunities through this celebration.

The ‘K-Walking’ programme went viral, the opposition attacked President Lee Jae Myung’s government, and the Army admitted it was ‘inappropriate’. Meghna Deka decodes: Is Seoul going soft on Kim Jong Un, or is this just one bad idea?

articles.title: Indian Cultural Pride Or Provocation? The Fine Line
articles.description: Indian celebrations abroad often become the centre of cultural and political controversy, especially on social media platforms. From a dance event in Houston to the backlash it triggered, where does cultural pride end and provocation begin? Why are Indian cultural expressions drawing outrage, and what does this reveal about the changing politics of identity and belonging? Is the backlash about discomfort over cultural differences, racism, or something deeper? On Beyond Borders Ananya Dasgupta examines the fine line between celebrating your heritage and being accused of provoking others.

articles.title: Vivek Oberoi reveals how 'Powerful Lobby' ruined his career, says he turned to alcohol and self-hate

He claimed he was dropped from films amid underworld threats and slipped into anger, heavy drinking and self-hate. The actor, known for ‘Company’ and ‘Saathiya’, is now part of Namit Malhotra’s ‘Ramayana’.

The biggest battle is unfolding around Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who faces renewed impeachment calls and investigations once Democrats take control of Congress.

articles.description: Fresh controversy has erupted at Tata Trusts after former trustee Mally Mistry challenged his removal from the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust. Mistry has questioned Venu Srinivasan's authority to vote against his reappointment, alleging that Srinivasan's own tenure had ended. He has also sought an inquiry into alleged commissions and conflict of interest issues within the trust. Krishna Gopalan, Business Today, brings you the latest developments, the governance concerns raised by Mistry and the possible implications for the Tata Group. With the upcoming Tata Sons board meeting adding to the developments, all eyes are now on how the dispute unfolds.
